content:
Ever since the iPhone 4 bumper case became a thing, bumper cases have remained popular, but good options are few. Rhinoshield offers a nice option for those who prefer a minimalist look.

Apple finally re-entered the bumper case market last year with the iPhone Air. There was initial hope that Apple would extend its bumper case to the iPhone 18 Pro (as it did with the clear case for the iPhone 11), but unfortunately that never materialized. While looking for alternatives, I came across Rhinoshield's Minimalist Impact Bumper.

Key details

The Impact Bumper fits similar to most bumper cases, with a relatively low lip around the screen but a slightly higher one on the back. One unique feature I really appreciate is the specially designed support structure that prevents the camera plateau and lenses from making direct contact with the surface the phone is placed on — which is especially useful for the 17 Pro and 18 Pro with their aluminum bodies. This design provides better protection than typical bumper cases and resolves the awkward wobble when the phone lies flat on a table.

However, the fit isn't quite what I hoped for. It feels a bit loose once installed, and the edges can be easily pried outward, which makes me worry about deformation over time. That said, I trust the phone won't easily fly out of the case when dropped (I've accidentally tested this). Still, the case is made of hard plastic rather than rubber, so hopefully it holds up long-term. Rhinoshield says the entire product uses just one type of material, making it 100% recyclable.

There are three color options available, all designed to complement the iPhone 18 Pro's body colors: white, blue, and black (sorry to those who liked the burgundy). I went with the blue, which is close to Glacier but not exactly the same.

The downsides

There are some drawbacks. My biggest complaint is that the buttons are quite hard to press. For some reason they went with an almost flush design, and combined with how the buttons are constructed, they feel mushy and unsatisfying to press.

The overall material choice can also be considered a drawback. For me, it doesn't feel as nice as the iPhone Air bumper case, though some people might actually prefer this texture. Personally, I find it more acceptable than typical TPU/rubber clear case materials. That said, this material, combined with the loose fit, seems particularly prone to attracting lint from pockets.

If you use Apple's Wrist Strap or Crossbody Strap, note that this case doesn't include the necessary attachment points.

Wrap-up

Rhinoshield's bumper case is far from perfect, and I'm still hoping Apple will extend its bumper case to other iPhone models. Ultimately, I decided to keep this case for one reason alone: it offers me a near caseless experience without worrying about the aluminum body getting scratched or dented. To my knowledge, this bumper case is typically only available on their own website, priced around $30, which after shipping comes close to Apple's $39 price. You can purchase the Rhinoshield Minimalist Impact Bumper here. (It occasionally shows up on Amazon too, so you might want to check there.)
